items.title: Practice, State, and the Two Marks: The Full Vocabulary of Entering a Concentration

items.zh: 何等為行？謂如所緣作種種行而入於定。謂麁行、靜行、病行、癰行、箭行、無常行等、若於彼彼三摩地中所有諸行。何等為狀？謂於諸定臨欲入時、便有此定相狀先起。由此狀故、彼自了知：我於如是如是相定，不久當入，或復正入。彼教授師由此狀故、亦了知彼不久當入如是如是相定。
items.en: What is "practice"? Taking up various modes of practice towards the object, and thereby entering concentration — coarse-practice, calm-practice, disease-practice, boil-practice, arrow-practice, impermanence-practice, and so on: whatever practices belong to each given concentration. What is "state"? When about to enter any concentration, the signs of that concentration arise first. By these signs, one knows for oneself: "in such-and-such a state, I shall soon enter, or am now entering." And by these same signs, one's teacher likewise knows that one will soon enter a concentration of such-and-such a state.

items.zh: 何等為相？謂二種相。一、所緣相，二、因緣相。所緣相者，謂分別體。由緣此故，能入諸定。
items.en: What is "mark"? Two kinds of mark: the object-mark and the causal mark. The object-mark is the discriminated substance [projected by the mind]; by taking this as object, one is able to enter the various concentrations.

items.title: The Causal Mark: What Concentration Actually Depends On

items.zh: 因緣相者，謂定資糧。由此因緣，能入諸定。謂隨順定教誡教授，積集諸定所行資糧，修俱行欲，厭患有心。於亂不亂審諦了知、及不為他之所逼惱。或人所作，或非人所作，或音聲所作，或功用所作。
items.en: The causal mark is the provisions for concentration; by this cause, one is able to enter the various concentrations. It means: rightly receiving the instruction and admonition that accord with concentration; accumulating the provisions concentration requires; cultivating the aspiration that accompanies practice; wearying of continued existence; accurately discerning whether the mind is scattered or not; and not being disturbed by others — whether the disturbance is caused by humans, by non-humans, by sound, or by material need.

items.title: Well-Adjusted vs. Not: The Difference Between a Forced Concentration and a Free One

items.zh: 云何調善？謂若三摩地猶為有行之所拘執，如水被持；或為法性之所拘執，不靜不妙，非安隱道，亦非證得心一趣性；此三摩地不名調善，不隨所樂安隱而住。與此相違，名為調善。
items.en: What is "well-adjusted"? If a concentration is still gripped by deliberate effort — like water held in a container — or is still gripped by [the worldly] dharma-nature, being neither quiescent nor subtle, not a secure path, and not yet the realisation of the mind's single course, then this concentration is not called well-adjusted; it does not rest securely as one wishes. The opposite of this is called well-adjusted.

items.zh: 云何猶為有行拘執？謂由誓願俱行思故，制伏外緣，持心於定。又於作意，要由功用方能運轉、不令內心於外流散。故作是說，如水被持。云何法性之所拘執？謂觀下地為麁法性，觀於上地為靜法性。
items.en: What is "still gripped by deliberate effort"? By the intention that accompanies one's vow, one subdues external conditions and holds the mind in concentration; and in applying attention, one must exert deliberate effort to keep it moving, so as not to let the mind scatter outward — hence the saying, "like water held [in a container]." What is "gripped by dharma-nature"? Contemplating a lower ground as coarse in nature, and a higher ground as calm in nature.

items.zh: 寂靜微妙，得安隱道，及能證得心一趣性，如五聖智三摩地中已略解釋。

items.title: Range: Why a Lower Attainment Cannot See a Higher One

items.zh: 云何所行？謂三摩地所行境界。由所得定，過此已上不能知故。如初靜慮，不能觀見第二靜慮。如是根度、數取趣度、亦不能知。
items.en: What is "range"? The domain within which a concentration operates. Whatever lies beyond the concentration one has attained cannot be known. Just as the first dhyāna cannot perceive the second, so too the range of faculties and the range of persons cannot be known [by those below them].

items.title: Eliciting: How Concentration Draws Forth Eloquence and Supreme Qualities

items.zh: 云何引發？謂能略攝廣文句義，及能成辦諸勝功德。
items.en: What is "eliciting"? Being able to condense and encompass vast phrasing and meaning into brief compass, and being able to accomplish the various supreme qualities.

items.title: Equal-Affection: The Wholesome Qualities That Actually Settle the Mind

items.zh: 云何等愛？謂慚、愧、愛、敬、信、正思惟、正念、正知、根護、戒護、及無悔等樂為最後。由隨樂故，心便得定。與此相違，名不等愛，云何等愛亦不等愛？謂如有一，於慚愧等少分成就，少不成就。謂具慚愧而無愛敬，乃至廣說。
items.en: What is "equal-affection"? Conscience, shame, love, reverence, faith, sound thought, mindfulness, clear knowing, guarding the faculties, guarding the precepts, and, last, freedom from regret leading to ease. By following that ease, the mind settles into concentration. The opposite of this is called "not equal-affection." What is "equal-affection yet also not"? Someone who accomplishes some of the above — conscience and the rest — and not others: possessing conscience and shame, say, but lacking love and reverence, and so on at length.

items.title: Increase, Decrease, and Method: The Last Three Aspects Named Briefly

items.zh: 云何為增？謂所得定轉復增長。云何為減？謂所得定還復退失。云何方便？謂趣彼二道。又止、舉、捨，當知如前止等相中已具分別。
items.en: What is "increase"? The concentration attained continuing to grow further. What is "decrease"? The concentration attained falling away again. What is "method"? Advancing by those two paths [calm and insight]. And calming, uplifting, and equanimity — know these as already fully distinguished in the marks of calming and the rest explained earlier.

items.title: Mistaking Advance for Decline: The Scripture on Distorted and Undistorted Practitioners

items.zh: 復次，如分別靜慮經言：有靜慮者，即於興等謂之為衰。乃至廣說。此中四轉，當知二時顛倒。謂於三摩地若退墮時，若勝進時，趣退及退，俱名為衰；趣勝進道及與勝進，俱名為興。
items.en: Furthermore, as the Sūtra Distinguishing Dhyāna says: "There are meditators who, at the very moment of flourishing, call it decline," and so on at length. Herein four permutations occur; know that both occasions [of flourishing and of decline] admit of distortion. When concentration either falls back or advances: heading towards decline and actual decline are both called "decline"; heading towards the path of advancement and actual advancement are both called "flourishing."

items.zh: 云何應知於三摩地進時顛倒？彼謂我今退失離生喜樂，我今退失勝三摩地。謂靜慮者勤修習故，心趣寂靜，隨捨行故。從初靜慮入於第二靜慮近分，然於此事不善了知。於此位中，初靜慮地喜樂已過，第二靜慮地中所有喜樂猶未能得。便作是念：我今退失離生喜樂。遂還從彼退攝其心。當知如是修靜慮者其心顛倒。
items.en: How should one recognise distortion at the moment of advancement in concentration? Such a one thinks: "I have now lost the joy-and-bliss born of seclusion; I have now lost my excellent concentration." For, through diligent cultivation, the meditator's mind moves towards quiescence, following the practice of equanimity: passing from the first dhyāna into the threshold of the second, yet not rightly understanding this — for at this stage, the first dhyāna's joy-and-bliss has already passed, and the second dhyāna's joy-and-bliss is not yet attained. So he thinks: "I have now lost the joy-and-bliss born of seclusion," and draws his mind back to that former state. Know that such a meditator's mind is distorted.

items.zh: 云何應知於三摩地退時顛倒？謂如有一，得初靜慮，為涅槃故，積集資糧。彼於涅槃，已得所修資糧圓滿；由此因緣，或由功用，或復任運，起如是想作意現前。由如是想作意故，於諸色中乃至識中，了知如病乃至無我。由如是想作意故，從此無間，因世間定所生喜樂不復現行。便作是念：我今退失定生利益，及所依止。遂還從彼退攝其心。如是當知修靜慮者於三摩地退失顛倒。云何當知於三摩地退失無倒？

blocks.text: Today's reading continues the gathering of scriptural terms about concentration. Two passages are especially useful for practitioners: how to understand visions in meditation, and a common mistake in which real progress feels like loss.

Entering a concentration involves its **practice**, its **state**, and its **marks**. The "state" is the signs that appear just before entry: "by these signs, one knows for oneself", and the teacher knows by observing.

The **object-mark** is "the discriminated substance": the image the mind holds. Venerable Miào Jìng applies this directly to visions: "The Buddha is an image of your discriminating mind; the Buddha doesn't really appear. If you know this, where is any demon?" Images in meditation are neither to be clung to nor feared; they are what the mind presents. This is consciousness-only as meditation advice.

Concentration depends on causes, including "not being disturbed by others". Venerable Miào Jìng adds a twist: when someone scolds you, "practise calm and insight right there; his scolding helps your practice advance." Disturbance can itself become the object.

A concentration may be "well adjusted" or "gripped by deliberate effort, like water held in place". Venerable Miào Jìng: water flows, so to control it you must enclose it in a bottle. A concentration still held by effort is not yet free. Another may be "gripped by dharma-nature": Master Cháng Bǎi: even at the peak of existence, one has not left the nature of the three realms.

A lower attainment cannot see a higher one ("range"). Concentration **elicits** eloquence and qualities. Venerable Miào Jìng: "People say 'hear one, know ten'; we do well to hear one and know one; but one who hears one and knows countless, that is eliciting."

"**Equal affection**" means conscience, shame, love, reverence, and faith held towards all good qualities equally. Venerable Miào Jìng: "love" here is wholesome aspiration. Master Cháng Bǎi adds the attitude it requires: "very down-to-earth; practise and you have it, don't and you don't."

"Method" is advancing by calming, uplifting, and equanimity at the right times. Venerable Miào Jìng: "Uplifting when you should calm, calming when you should uplift, calming or uplifting when you should leave it in equanimity: it won't work." (Day 85's four adjustments.)

A precise observation. Passing from the first dhyāna towards the second, "the first dhyāna's joy-and-bliss has already passed, and the second's is not yet attained", and the meditator thinks, "I've lost my concentration." This is distortion: real progress felt as loss. Venerable Miào Jìng traces it to refusing guidance: "'I'll practise myself; I won't listen to you.' One is progressing but does not know it." A teacher who knows the map can tell a student that the dryness is a transition, not a failure.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what is the "state" of entering concentration?
options: the signs of a concentration arising just before entry — oneself knows one will soon enter, and the teacher knows by them too
quiz.why: "When about to enter any concentration, the signs of that concentration arise first. By these signs, one knows for oneself … And by these same signs, one's teacher likewise knows." Master Cháng Bǎi: sensations of heaviness, roughness, smoothness tell the teacher which dhyāna is near.

quiz.q: The object-mark is "the discriminated substance." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say about seeing the Buddha in meditation?
options: the Buddha is an image of your discriminating mind, not truly appearing — knowing this, where is any demon?
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "The Buddha is an image of your discriminating mind — the Buddha doesn't really appear." "If you fear going astray in meditation, knowing this, where could any demon be?" Master Cháng Bǎi: imagining a skeleton makes it appear.

quiz.q: The causal mark includes "not being disturbed by others." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say to do when insulted?
options: practice calm and insight right there — his insult helps your practice advance
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "When he scolds you, practice calm and insight right there; his scolding helps your calm-and-insight power progress." Serving food or cooking also "accumulates the provisions concentration requires."

quiz.q: A concentration "gripped by deliberate effort, like water held." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain the image?
options: water flows; you must enclose it in a bottle to control it
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Water flows; you must enclose it, put it in a bottle, and control it." The text: by vow-driven intention one holds the mind, attention moving only by effort — hence "like water held." Like learning calligraphy: poor at first, fluent later.

quiz.q: "Equal-affection" includes conscience, shame, love, reverence, faith. What does Venerable Miào Jìng say "love" is here?
options: wholesome aspiration — delighting in all good dharmas; loving all these equally is equal-affection
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Love here is wholesome aspiration — delighting in all good dharmas." "Equal-affection means loving equally." The text: ending in freedom from regret and ease, the mind settles.

quiz.q: "Method" is advancing by two paths, with calming, uplifting, equanimity. What happens if they're mistimed, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: uplifting when calm is needed, calm when uplift is needed, calm or uplift when equanimity is needed — it won't work
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Uplifting when you should calm, calming when you should uplift, calming or uplifting when you should rest in equanimity — that won't do." Calm and insight are the method. Master Cháng Bǎi: when agitated, calm; when dull, uplift; when both are good, rest in equanimity.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what is distortion at the time of advancement?
options: passing into the second dhyāna's threshold, the first's joy gone and the second's not yet come, one thinks "I've lost the joy of seclusion" and pulls back
quiz.why: "At this stage, the first dhyāna's joy-and-bliss has already passed, and the second dhyāna's joy-and-bliss is not yet attained. So he thinks: 'I have now lost the joy-and-bliss born of seclusion,' and draws his mind back." Master Cháng Bǎi: he thinks he's regressed, but he's advancing.
